newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Manila suspends grain imports - traders.
newsitem.headline: Manila suspends grain imports - traders.

text.p: Philippine grain importers have suspended grain imports following the sharp fall of the peso against the U.S. dollar, traders and industry officials said on Monday.
"All bets are off," one trader said. "The Filipinos will not be buying until they see some calm return to the exchange rate."

"They've suspended grain imports, especially those for wheat. Most of the companies have good grain inventories so they will not be coming in for a while," said a dealer who does a lot of business from the Philippines.
Traders said the pounding taken by the Philippine peso, effectively devalued on Friday, drove almost all the country's flour mills out of the market.
The dealers estimated the Philippines would probably stay out of the market for at least one week and possibly two.
The peso hit a low of 29.75 to the dollar during trading on Monday.

The Philippines is the second leading buyer of U.S. wheat in Southeast Asia. It bought around 2.1 million tonnes of wheat in the 1996/97 (June/May) marketing year, of which 1.8 million tonnes came from the United States.
